project_scope.selection_mode: comparison-first across canonical local Oenothera plus B061 expansion
project_scope.note: Modern Oenothera includes former Gaura and Calylophus concepts. B061 adds three strict target-zone PASS species and retains O. biennis + O. filiformis as range HOLDs.

study_strategy.warning: Do not rely on petal color alone. Modern Oenothera contains very different-looking former Gaura and Calylophus lineages.

quick_key.if: large radial pink/white 4-petaled flowers on a spreading rhizomatous plant
tall airy perennial with former-Gaura flowers and long exserted stamens
tall densely velveteen annual with extremely tiny flowers
annual with larger white former-Gaura flowers and chunky 4-lobed fruit
flat stemless rosette with large yellow flower on an extremely long sharply 4-angled tube
low yellow evening primrose with broader cut-lobed leaves
very narrow linear leaves + yellow sundrop flowers + strongly 4-angled buds
perennial limestone gaura with white flowers fading pink/red

diagnostic_science_review_20261009.scope_note: Comparison enrichment only; no canonical installation or gallery backfill. Genus project_scope's eight-species B061 cohort is historical, NOT the full canonical roster. Manifest audit on 2026-10-09: 17 installed Oenothera IDs. Sheet Genus Study Index's 20 curated rows include synonyms/parent concepts; those are source rows, not 20 unique canonical species.
look_here_first: Sort the specimen by flower architecture: classic radial primrose, minute-flowered former-Gaura spike, showier former-Gaura spike, or yellow sundrop (former Calylophus).
Inspect flower and bud side views, including hypanthium, sepal tips, and inferior ovary; do not classify from petal color.
For former-Gaura spikes compare flowering-axis hairs at magnification, open-flower diameter, and mature indehiscent fruit proportions.
For sundrops compare lower versus upper leaves, bud tip length, sepal keels, hypanthium, and stigma; verify the subspecies concept before merging historical names.
Confirm using mature capsule/fruit and multiple organs. A single worn flower, color, habitat, or photo without scale is not a safe separator.

pair: Oenothera capillifolia subsp. berlandieri (source alias Calylophus berlandieri)
comparison_groups.title: Former Calylophus subspecies identity — DO NOT AUTO-MERGE

diagnostics.detail: POWO accepts O. capillifolia subsp. berlandieri for Calylophus berlandieri Spach; separately accepts O. capillifolia subsp. capillifolia. Species-level O. capillifolia learner is not evidence of subspecies identity.

UT Williamson County subsp. capillifolia has narrow leaves about 20–75 × 1.2–3 mm, conspicuously four-sided buds, and 28–40 mm open flowers; these are an anchor, not a validated dichotomous separator from berlandieri.
FNA gives 30–80 cm erect/ascending stems, leaves 2.5–9 × 0.2–1 cm, free bud tips 0.5–4 mm, and keeled sepals. These ranges overlap some sundrops and are not an independent diagnosis without full key.

unreliable: A dark purple floral tube or stigma occurs in FNA-documented subsp. capillifolia populations from Hays and neighboring counties: DO NOT use dark tube/stigma color to force berlandieri.
Texas nativity at the species/subspecies level does not establish a project three-county native PASS for an unidentified source record.
Source label 'Calylophus berlandieri' must not automatically be attached to a photograph labeled subsp. capillifolia.
photo_roles: Voucher-linked flowering plant with source-confirmed subspecies
Matched stem habit and lower/upper leaf series with scale
Bud side macro measuring free sepal tips and keel
Hypanthium and stigma close-ups, labeled as variable-color support only

comparison_groups.title: Historical Calylophus name trap

diagnostics.detail: POWO treats Calylophus drummondiana Spach as a synonym of Oenothera serrulata Nutt.; Oenothera drummondii Hook. is a separate accepted species. The source spelling 'Calylophus drummondii' is not resolved to either without original voucher/taxon ID.
Preserve source-pool learner admission but mark exact mapping HOLD; do not create a new canonical card, silently fold the name into O. serrulata, or infer native PASS.

unreliable: Shared epithet 'drummondii' is not evidence of synonymy; spellings and author citations matter.
Common names and generic yellow flower images cannot resolve this historical source label.
photo_roles: Original source observation screenshot or herbarium voucher showing taxon ID and author
Voucher-linked leaf, bud, flower and capsule series once mapping resolved

comparison_groups.title: Stemless long-tube rosette

diagnostics.detail: Acaulescent flat basal rosette with stem concealed at ground level, unlike tall leafy stems of many other primroses.
Very long, sharply four-angled hypanthium to approximately 97 mm in UT Williamson County description; trace it all the way to the inferior ovary.
UT Williamson County detailed dissection reports four stamens; use as a corroborating dissected-flower feature, not a stand-alone identification when counts conflict across sources.

unreliable: Yellow petals and lobed leaves are shared by multiple Oenothera.
Stamen counts from a photo or non-dissected worn flower are error-prone.
photo_roles: Full basal rosette with scale and stem position labeled
Whole intact flower side view with ruler spanning hypanthium
Flower dissection clearly exposing stamens and inferior ovary
